verses.text: By the time the seventh month came, the Israelites were in their towns. Then the people came together in Jerusalem, united as one.

Jeshua son of Jozadak got to work with his fellow priests, along with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives. They built the altar of the God of Israel so they could offer burnt offerings there, just as it was written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
They were scared of the peoples around them, but they set the altar on its base anyway. There they made burnt offerings to the LORD every morning and evening.
They celebrated the Festival of Booths as written, bringing the required number of burnt offerings each day, just as the rule for that day called for.
After that came the regular burnt offering, the offerings for the new moons and all the LORD’s appointed holy festivals, and the gifts people freely chose to offer to the LORD.
They started giving burnt offerings to the LORD on the first day of the seventh month. The foundation of the LORD’s temple still hadn’t been laid.
They paid the stoneworkers and carpenters. They gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, as King Cyrus of Persia had authorized.

In the second month of the second year after they came to God’s house in Jerusalem, the work got underway. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, their fellow priests and Levites, and everyone who’d come back to Jerusalem from exile started the work. They put Levites twenty and older in charge of the work on the LORD’s house.

Jeshua stood with his sons and brothers, along with Kadmiel and his sons, the descendants of Judah. They supervised the workers in God’s house together with Henadad’s sons, their sons, and their fellow Levites.

When the builders laid the foundation of the LORD’s temple, the priests took their places in their robes with trumpets. The Levites descended from Asaph held cymbals. They were there to praise the LORD as King David of Israel had directed.

They sang back and forth, praising and thanking the LORD: “He is good! His faithful love for Israel lasts forever!” Then everybody let out a huge shout of praise to the LORD because the foundation of his house was in place.
But many of the older priests, Levites, and family heads had seen the first house. When they saw the foundation of this house being laid, they cried out loud. Many others shouted for joy.
Nobody could tell the sound of the cheering from the sound of the crying. The people were so loud that you could hear them far away.
